Republican Policy Retreat

Donald Trump addresses House Republicans at annual policy retreat in Florida. Read the transcript here.

Hungry For More?

Luckily for you, we deliver. Subscribe to our blog today.

Speaker 1 (00:02):

Speaker Mike Johnson, Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Majority Whip Tom Emmer, and Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain.

Mike Johnson (00:31):

Thank you all so much. Have a seat for just a moment. It is so good to be here again, at Doral, President Trump's amazing property. How about a round of applause for this incredible venue, and the Congressional Institute we're so grateful for bringing us all together, as they have done for many years now. This is the best time to be together. It's the best place to be together. We have so much to celebrate. When we were here just last year, we were talking about being on the edge, on the verge of the dawn of a new golden era in America, and my friends, that is exactly what we are in the middle of now, the new golden era, new golden age.

(01:14)
And that's because when voters gave us this mandate in the election of 2024, they wanted us to fix everything. As you know, every metric of public policy was an absolute disaster. And they gave the President of the United States, this president, 75 million popular votes. He won the electoral college decisively. And along the way, and in large part because of his coattails, we had the largest popular vote ever in history for House Republicans, almost 75 million votes. That's right. So we came in with a mandate, and we came in with an agenda, and we began to work very hard. We worked hand in hand with the president to move that agenda along, the America First agenda. And the record of the first year of the Trump Administration in the last couple of months has been promises made, promises kept, because we take the responsibility that we have been given by the people seriously.

(02:06)
It's a restoration of common sense. We are bringing America back again, and it's largely because of the leadership of the gentleman that I'll introduce to you in a moment. He is the most active president, the most energized president, the most successful president, I believe, in my lifetime, and he's proven it over and over and over. And part of it is because he doesn't sleep, thankfully. He's got so much to do, and I know that because I get calls from him at 2:00 AM and 7:00 AM, sometimes in the same day. He doesn't require a lot of sleep, thankfully, and he is the man for the moment. His achievements are incalculable. History will record that this president came at exactly the right time, on the eve of the 250th anniversary of the greatest nation in the history of the world, the most free, most successful, most powerful, most benevolent nation that has ever been.

(02:57)
And we understand, and he understands, that it's not guaranteed. He understands that we have to fight for it every single day, and he does that every single day. Just in the last week, my friends, anytime this president sees a problem, he jumps right in to fix it. I've been involved in just what I've been involved in the last few days with him. Several days back, earlier in the week, he recognized that the growth of AI, and the new tech and the need for data centers around the country, and new energy sources. He pulled together all the leaders in the industry. He's the only person that has the gravitas to be able to do that, and he pulled them all together and they signed the rate payer protection pledge, to make sure that energy prices continue to go down and don't rise, even though the demand... That's right. It's a big thing.

(03:47)
And then a couple of days later, we're working hard in the House, and the House leadership team's doing all of our thing, and I get summoned back to the White House. What is it now? Well, the president needs to save colleges and universities. The NIL, the Name, Image, and Likeness madness has really gotten out of control, and the president's decided that he's the man to fix it. And he is. And so he summoned us all together. And I mean, we had, you probably saw, 60 of the biggest names in college sports and athletics, and college administration, university administration, all summoned to the White House for a productive meeting to get the SCORE Act and our solutions done and finished up. A few days later, I turn on the TV. I'm trying to rest a little bit. The president doesn't. Why? Because now he's back down here in South Florida, and he has brought together and created the New Hemisphere Initiative to take out narco terrorists and secure the hemisphere.

(04:40)
This security for the Americas, it's a new initiative that he alone has conceived. This president never stops. There's so much to fix. We have the right man for this hour. History will record one of the most consequential presidencies in the history of this extraordinary country. We are all blessed to be a part of it, to work alongside him in the legislative branch, and to get this done for America. We will continue to do that as we head in to the most important midterm election of our lifetimes. We all know that. Without further ado, my friends, I want to present to you not just our host and the property owner, but the 45th and the 47th President of the United States, Donald J. Trump.

Speaker 2 (05:25):

From the lakes of Minnesota to the hills of Tennessee, across the plains of Texas, from sea to shining sea, from Detroit down to Houston, and New York to LA, where there's pride in every American heart, and it's time we stand and say that I'm proud to be an American, where at least I know I'm free. And I won't forget the men who died, who gave that right to me, and I gladly stand up next to you and defend her still today, because there ain't no doubt I love this land. God bless the USA. And I'm proud to be an American, and I won't forget the men who died, who gave that right to me. And I gladly stand up next to you and defend her still today, because there ain't no doubt I love this land. God bless the USA.

President Trump (07:09):

Wow, a lot of friends. Sit down, we have a little time. Just everybody, thank you very much. And our great speaker, Speaker Johnson. And hello to the men and women of one of the most consequential Republican majorities in history. It's not a big majority, but it's just about the most consequential. The job you've done is incredible. And they are members that are warriors, and really people that are for the American people, and that's why you're doing well, and I think that's why we're going to continue to do well. We're fighting a little tradition. Historically, the person that wins, Democrat or Republican, wins the presidency, for whatever reason, it doesn't work out, but we've done a lot. I don't know. I think we've done... I think we had the best first year of any president ever, and that includes you. You came along with me, and you've made it happen.

(08:02)
So with your help and hard work, we're making America great again, and we're doing it much faster than we thought. And it's better, stronger, and our country is doing really well, I mean, at a level that nobody thought. We took a little excursion because we felt we had to do that to get rid of some evil, and I think you'll see it's going to be a short-term excursion. How good is our military, right? Amazing. How good? Short-term. Short-term. Thank you. They're great.

(08:43)
You know, we all together, in my first term, we rebuilt our military, and I didn't know I'd be using it so much in the second term, but we have a military like no other, it's not even close. But I especially want to recognize the rest of our amazing House Republican leadership team, and so many of my friends that are congressmen, some senators, we have some great people in this room, but including a majority leader, a real brave guy, because I know the real story. I was there that night with him in the hospital, when he was given a very small chance of living by a doctor who was very good, by a wife who was desperately in love with him. She cried so much. Because I've seen the other too, I've seen guys at the end of the line, the wives aren't exactly shaken up. When they don't cry, when they have no tears, or any sign of tears, this is not a good sign of a great marriage. But he must have a great marriage because she was just devastated she was going to lose her guy. But it worked out.

(09:51)
The doctor said more blood was put into him than he's ever seen. He was in big trouble. I looked at him that night and I said goodbye to him, but he made it. He was brave, and look at the way he fought back for so many different things. Steve Scalise. And we have another one, Tom Emmer, who I really got to know over the last few years. And I'll tell you, he's a winner. He's a champion, with another great wife. We got good wives up in there. Let's say great wife, fine husband. But Tom is just a real champion and a winner, and you have a problem, you go to him. He gets it settled. So thank you very much, Tom. Great job. You've done a great job. And our conference chairwoman is Lisa McClain, and we all know Lisa. Don't get on her wrong side, it can be a very, very bad experience. Thank you very much. Great job, Lisa. Great job.

(10:55)
And a very special thanks. You broke a record, this is over 20 million, that's the biggest of these type of events that there's ever been, actually by a lot. You didn't just break it, you broke it by a lot, so I want to congratulate you. But there's just great spirit. The Republican Party has fantastic spirit. The level I don't think has been seen before. I really don't. We have to get a couple of people on board, which at least one case is virtually impossible. I wonder who that might be. Sick person. But I want to say a very special thanks to everyone at the Congressional Institute for helping organize this event. This has been amazing. And over the past nine days, we've been reminded of how vital our Republican majorities are. And it's America's future. We're really fighting because these people, you saw the other night at the State of the Union, you saw these people, they wouldn't stand for a mother who just lost her daughter by having her throat slit from behind.

(12:07)
They wouldn't stand for the helicopter pilot who just got the congressional Medal of Honor for landing safely in Venezuela, a helicopter with a lot of soldiers on that, lot of soldiers on that helicopter. And he was able to land it safely, and his leg was practically ripped off. And for those people that know about helicopters, you land them pretty much with your legs, right, Tom? You land him with the legs, and he was in bad shape, and he got that... Not only landed, he landed in exactly the right spot at exactly... As blood was pouring down the aisle, which didn't make all of those soldiers in the back feel too good. They're looking at a pilot as bleeding out. But they didn't want to stand for that. They didn't want to stand for a 100-year-old soldier who had left a legacy of bravery. Everybody talked about it for years, and it was time for him to get the Congressional Medal of Honor. They didn't want to stand for him.

(13:06)
There's something wrong with those people, and we can't let them ever be in a position where they can lead this country again, or destroy this country again, because we almost lost this country. This country was close to being lost. The representatives in this room provided the pivotal votes in securing a record $1 trillion for the United States military this year. And now the world is witnessing the importance of that investment, with one of the most complex and stunning operations ever conducted, and it's Operation Epic Fury. That's a great name, isn't it, Epic Fury. That's even better than Midnight Hammer, which was pretty good too, right? That was where we'd knocked out their nuclear potential.

(13:56)
That was a big day, because if we didn't do that, they would've had a nuclear weapon within two weeks, and I think we'd be in a lot different situation. And then you had, of course, what they did in Venezuela, how that was. That was just so far, so good. We've done a real job. We've got all good ones. If you go back and you look at Afghanistan with Biden, one of the worst. I think the most embarrassing moment in the history of our country. If you look at what happened with Jimmy Carter, also with Iran, but if you look at what happened with the helicopters and the hostages, it cost them the election. It was what a mess. The world respects us right now more than they have ever respected us before. And because of Republicans, you people in Congress, the United States has by far the strongest and most powerful military on the face of the Earth. We're the strongest military anywhere in the earth, and now

President Trump (15:00):

Everybody understands it. Together, with our Israeli partners, we're crushing the enemy in an overwhelming display of technical skill and military force. Iran's drone and missile capability is being utterly demolished. The Navy is gone. It's all lying at the bottom of the ocean. 46 ships. Can you believe it? Fact, I got a little upset with our people. I said, "What quality of ship?" "Excellent, sir. Top of the line." I said, "Why didn't we just capture the ship? We could have used it. Why did we sink them?" They said, "It's more fun to sink them." I said, "That's a ..." They like sinking them better. They say it's safer to sink them. I guess it's probably true. But think of it. We knocked out 46, and actually took three and a half days. Their terrorist leaders are gone or counting down the minutes until they will be gone. Think of it.

(15:54)
We had leaders, and they're gone. Then we had new leaders, and they're gone. And now nobody has any idea who the people are that are going to be the head of the country. And we'll not relent until the enemy is totally and decisively defeated as ... And remember, Iran did so many bad things. They were really ... If you look at Soleimani, who was taken out, as you know that, by you know who. But if you look at Soleimani, the father of the roadside ... You call it a roadside bomb because most people don't understand the different terms. It was where they plant bombs in roads. As you drive by, happily drive by, the bomb goes off. And no matter how strong the armament, it just kills the people. Or you lose your arms, legs, and face. And those bombs got worse and worse, and he got happier and happier.

(16:50)
We took him out. That was a big thing because he was the head. It might've been a much different story. They may have been much more capable than they are had he lived because he was capable. He was vicious, violent, and capable. But we got rid of him first term. And we did so many things. We've done so many things. But as you know, on Saturday, I traveled to Dover Air Force Base to be with the families of six fallen warriors as they returned to American soil. And I know that everyone in this room joins me in sending our prayers and eternal gratitude to the families of those great heroes. Those families are incredible families. Devastating to me. Hardest thing to do. I've done it a lot. The hardest thing to do is to go to Dover because Dover is where, for the most part, a lot of the fallen, the warriors, the great young people that have died in war, they seem to mostly go to Dover.

(17:48)
They come home to Dover. Dover does a great job of handling things. They have men assigned to the family. They have men and women, that are incredible, assigned to the families. It's a beautiful thing, but it's also a very sad thing. But they all said one thing to me, "Make sure you win, sir. Make sure you win." They weren't playing games.

(18:12)
They want to make sure they said it. Everybody said it. They were separate, but everybody said the same thing. "Make sure you win." We will. We've already won in many ways, but we haven't won enough. We go forward more determined than ever to achieve ultimate victory that will end this long-running danger once and for all. 47 years. It should have been done a long time ago. World would have been a different place had some president had the courage to go and do it. They should have done it many, many times. They had many opportunities. The United States of America is the greatest and most exceptional nation in human history and will not be threatened by evil terrorists and lunatics any longer. We just can't do that. And when I always talk about how great our nation is, I don't know. I don't consider our nation very great for four years under Biden.

(19:01)
We were a laughing stock all over the world. We were a laughing stock. So I say, "Great, great, great," but I don't know. When you look at what happened with so many different things, the open border, 25 million people, many of them very bad people, pouring into our country with open borders that just said, "Come on in. Come on in. Makes no difference." They emptied their jails into our country.

(19:25)
11,888 murders, 50% of which murdered more than one person. The drug dealers came in. The mentally insane came in. They emptied their mental institutions. They emptied their insane asylum. That's a step above a mental institution. They emptied them all right into our country. And we've done a great job of doing what we've done. Think of it. We have the lowest crime rate that we've ever had. We have the lowest murder rate in 125 years. And we're saddled with all of the problems of the criminals that were let in. Look, they're smart people. I know the people that run those countries, every one of them, and they're all streetwise, very smart. And I would do exactly the same thing. They emptied their jails into our country. I said that was going to happen when I heard that they were having open borders. I didn't believe that they were going to have ... When I realized that they actually were going to have open borders, I said, "We're going to have every person in jail. We're going to have every drug dealer. We're going to have all these countries all over the world." The Congo, they emptied their jails. All the way from the Congo to all parts of South America, Asia, they sent in their people in jail, murderers. Some of the worst people on earth got sent into our country. And I'll tell you what, ICE is unbelievable, what they have to put up with and how tough they have to be. That goes for border patrol and it goes for law enforcement, our law enforcement people. But sadly, even as our service members are fighting bravely to protect America abroad, the Democrat minority in Congress is deliberately sabotaging our national security at home. And you're going through it right now, fellas. You're going through ... It's not even believable. We should be very safe right now, especially when we're attacking somebody that's evil, bad intention.

(21:23)
But last week, 53 House Democrats voted against a resolution affirming that Iran remains the world's number one state sponsor of terror. How would ... How would do that? Almost every act, whether it's Hamas or Hezbollah, no matter what, you take a look, it's Iran or Iran sponsored. And even more outrageously, as we speak, Democrats have shut down the Department of Homeland Security. They've got it shut down. Do you believe it? Right now. Because they care more about amnesty for illegal alien criminals than about protecting the lives of American [inaudible 00:21:59]. Take a look at it. The American citizen is being scoffed at by Democrats. It doesn't make sense. None of their stuff makes sense to me. When they sat and they wouldn't stand up for incredible people, they just refused to clap, stand up. By the end of the speech, by the way, they were all standing because somebody was passing them, "No, you people are getting killed tonight."

(22:26)
They'd stand up for everything I was saying at the end. That last half hour, they were standing up for things that they shouldn't have stood up for because they got the word. "You're getting killed tonight. Stand up and clap for the woman that just lost her daughter, please, to a violent criminal." But Democrats must vote immediately to reopen the Department of Homeland Security so that we have the resources to keep America safe.

(22:56)
And under our pro America, pro worker, pro family agenda, our country is winning again and America is respected again. And I think we have a country that's as hot as it's ever been ever before, maybe hotter. And I say it all the time. The king of Saudi Arabia said it to me better than anybody could say it. I get along with him very well. Very smart person. He said, "A year and a half ago, your country was dead. Absolutely dead. We never thought it was coming back. And now you have the hottest country anywhere in the world." It's true. We're the hottest country anywhere in the world by far. And that's before we showed off our military strength with Venezuela and now with Iran. Iran was supposed to be this big powerful country. We wrapped the hell out of them. And I don't know when they cry uncle, but they should have cried it two days ago, right?

(23:53)
But they don't have anything left. In our country, inflation is plummeting. Incomes are rising. The economy is surging. Our border is the most secure at any time in American history. And the murder rate is the lowest in 125 years. That's before my father was born. My father was born six years later than that. I don't know if he'd like me to say that. Never liked to talk about his age. He said, "Don't talk about that." But think about 125 years ago, 1900, the year 1900. The stock market has set 53 all-time record highs since the election, and it's going to go a lot higher soon as we get rid of this stuff that we're doing right now, that we really had no choice. I think I asked people, I said, "Would you rather do this or would you rather go along nice and smoothly, but eventually have a catastrophe the likes of which perhaps the world has never seen?" And just about everybody says, except for lunatics, said, "No, you had to get it done. Should have been done a long time ago."

(24:54)
The average 401(k) is up almost $35,000. Think of that. It's at the best they've ever done. And I think you're going to see some real numbers when this gets ... Because this was always a dark cloud hanging over, not only Israel, which was going to get wiped out. If we didn't do that B-2 attack, Israel would've been wiped out. They would've had a nuclear weapon within two weeks after that. And even now, I think they were looking to take over the Middle East because when you look, and we have pretty good proof, all of those missiles that were so stupidly aimed at Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, they were all aimed, and others, at countries that were sort of like, "Leave us alone." They were all right. They were sort of neutral, but they weren't doing ... All of a sudden, they're getting hit with missiles. And they could have gone one of two ways.

(25:44)
They could have gone toward their side, like, "We're with you," or they could have gone with our side. And they really went with our side and they've helped us and they've been a big force, but they got hit. But they were going to be hit with us. Had we not done the B-2 raid, and have we not done this one where we said, "Nope, it's time to go in. We have to go in, have no choice," number one, if we didn't go in, they would have come in after us because I see the Democrats trying to justify it, and they're failing because the voter on the street is saying it. You got to be kidding. But I see where they're going, where they're always saying, "No, no, there was no reason." Well, I'll give you the best reason of all. Within a week, they were going to attack us, 100%.

(26:26)
They were ready. They had all these missiles, far more than anyone thought, and they were going to attack us, but they were going to attack all of the Middle East and Israel. And if they had a nuclear weapon, they would have used it on Israel. And this was going to be a major attack on all ... They had all of those missile sites and all those launches, that we got rid of about 80% of them right now, by the way. Got rid of most of the ... See, it's died down to a trickle. There are very few launchers left. What our military has done is amazing. They wiped out almost 20%, maybe 22, 23%, but the rest are going very quickly. And the missiles have been largely knocked out. The drones have been knocked down. And we're hitting where they make the drones. We know them all. And we're knocking the hell out of that now where they manufacture the drones.

(27:14)
A lot of work, a lot of brilliant work, but we're going to have a much safer world as soon as it's finished, and it's going to be finished pretty quickly. With the help of our House Republican majority, we passed the largest tax cuts in American history. We have to be talking about it.

(27:30)
And with the great Big Beautiful Bill, we delivered no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, and no tax on Social Security for our great seniors. And we did something else, which is great that nobody ever talks about, Tom, and we have to talk about it. We made interest on auto loans fully deductible. That's never happened. We've never had that. Rich people always get deductions, but middle income people, people that have to struggle a little bit, never did, but now they can deduct the interest paid against their taxes. We have one little proviso, and I put this on, it's very important, only if the car is made in America, right? That's going to have a huge impact. That's going to have a huge impact. We passed the Trump Accounts to give every child in America a head start on the American dream, and that's so good. It was ... I'll tell you, the Dell family, Dell computer, he put up $6,250,000,000. Think of it. He started with very little, nothing, very, very little. Started making computers on his bed. And he said, "Yeah. People started liking them better than the ones from the store." And he never stopped. And he can write a check for 6 billion, 250 million. And his incredible wife, Susan, they said it's the best thing they've ever done. He's so proud. He's going to do it again, going to do more. And we have a lot of other people. A lot of very rich people are doing it. A lot of people that aren't so rich are doing it. They're doing it for their kids, but it's turning out ... So a young child turns 18 or 21. And all of a sudden, they have $100,000 in the bank. What a difference that is between having that and having nothing.

(29:25)
And it could be more than that, could be a lot more, depending on what happens with the world. And we passed 100% expensing and bonus depreciation on all new equipment, factory construction, and investments. And that's what made our first term. We had the greatest economy in the history of our country in the first term. And this one's going to blow it away. Again, we had a little pause, but it's not a very big pause. With your help, we also passed the largest regulation cuts in American history, ending the Green New scam, one of the greatest scams in history, and massively increasing

President Trump (30:00):

Increasing production of American oil, natural gas, and clean, beautiful coal. We brought coal back. You're not allowed to say coal without, "Clean, beautiful." Got to be clean, beautiful. China uses coal, they're building about 65 massive coal plants right now. Great respect for China, but they make all the windmills, right? The only thing they don't do is use the windmills, they make them. But try finding wind farms in China, there aren't too many of them. In my State of the Union address, I laid out an ambitious agenda that should be our roadmap this year. And it's starting with lowering the cost of living. They gave us a mess, we inherited a mess, an absolute mess. And the mess was many things. They were bad with our military. They were bad with everything. I mean, I said name one thing that they did right, they can't name one thing, but they also gave us very high prices, and then they said the word, affordability.

(31:04)
That's the first time I ever heard it, they said, "Affordability." My first day in office, they said, "Affordability." They're the ones that caused the problem, but we're really bringing down prices big. Do you notice you don't hear that word anymore, Mike?

Mike (31:15):

No.

Speaker 3 (31:15):

No.

President Trump (31:16):

They don't say it anymore because we've brought down prices so much. So our message is simple, Democrats created the high prices and our policies are totally ending them and they're ended and we're doing better. We're even bringing them down further. They'll be way down. If you go back into the last period, I would say, I think it's two and a half months, 1.7% inflation, three months, 1.45% inflation. Think of that. Whereas they had the single highest inflation in the history of our country. Now, I always say this, they say 48 years, because I don't want the fake news to get me on this, they say it wasn't history, it was 48 years, that the inflation was the highest in 48 years.

(32:06)
But I don't know, in some ways, 48 years sounds even worse, because it's very specific. But they had the highest inflation, probably in history. But in 48 years, we inherited that. One of the first targets must be the crushing healthcare. We have to crush and take over the healthcare situation, which we can do. For the first time, we can do it. Since the passage of the Unaffordable Care Act, big insurance companies have gotten rich, they've made money like practically no other companies have made, with our government giving them hundreds of billions of dollars, and their stock price is soaring to up to 1,000%, 1,200%, 1,600%, and even 1,700%. The government gave them, essentially, trillions of dollars. And I want that money to be paid to the person, not to the insurance company, and let them go out and buy their own healthcare. And people love it. People love it.

(33:14)
You'll get better healthcare at a much lower cost, and they'll be sort of part of the system. But the money we spend on, is so much, we spent numbers that nobody could even believe. But the healthcare companies, because the Democrats are owned by the insurance companies, remember that. And so they have a problem. That's why it's hard to get it fixed, because they are totally owned and controlled by the healthcare, by the insurance companies, healthcare insurance, but the insurance companies themselves. So when you want to do something that's good for the people, but bad for the insurance companies, it's very, very hard for them to go in a different way.

(33:55)
Now, Republicans never do that kind of thing, right? You're owned by nobody, right? Nobody. See, young girl up here, say, "Yes." Some of them are a little bit shaky, but they're Republicans, we love them. We love them anyway, right, Mike? But they are owned by those big, powerful insurance companies that are making a fortune and it's hard to get them to do the right thing. They know what the right thing is. So we want the money to be paid directly to the people and let the people go out and buy their own healthcare. And people love it. They love it. We can own the issue. For the first time ever, Republicans can own that issue.

(34:36)
